listen.script: Think of inflation as a slow leak in your wallet. Put another way, the same amount of money buys a little less every year. That's why keeping cash under your bed isn't the smartest way to save.

options: A slow leak in a wallet

listen.script: When the city spread into the desert, most new homes were far from shops and offices. As a consequence, nearly every family needed two cars, and this, in turn, made the morning traffic much worse.

listen.script: That's an interesting question. It's hard to generalise, but I'd say most young people still value family traditions. Where they differ from their grandparents is that they adapt them to fit modern life, rather than following every detail.
listen.q: How are young people different from their grandparents, according to the speaker?
options: They have no interest in traditions.
They adapt traditions to modern life.
They follow every detail of traditions.

read.passage: In many coastal cities, coral reefs are under growing pressure. Scientists say the damage stems from several causes at once. Rising sea temperatures can trigger coral bleaching, in which corals lose the tiny algae that give them colour and food. Pollution and plastic waste add to the stress, and badly managed tourism can break fragile reefs. Admittedly, tourism also brings money that can be used for protection. That said, experts warn that the benefits disappear if visitor numbers are not controlled. What this means, in practice, is that a reef can only be saved if the causes are tackled together. Some projects now combine strict rules for divers, regular clean-ups and research into heat-resistant coral. Red Sea coral is of particular interest, because some of it appears to tolerate warmer water better than coral elsewhere.

options: Corals lose the algae that give them colour and food.

qs.q: What does the writer concede about tourism?
options: It has no effect on reefs.
It can bring money for protection.

qs.q: According to the passage, how can a reef be saved?
options: By tackling all the causes together

qs.q: Why is Red Sea coral of special interest?
options: It is the most colourful in the world.
Some of it seems to tolerate warmer water.
It is not affected by pollution.
